answer: A reputation stake tied to verifiable work resists Sybil attacks: each agent must lock a deposit and complete costly, checkable tasks before trading, so creating thousands of fake identities means paying thousands of deposits. Like light through a prism, one identity splits into many colours only if each colour is paid for; a jetty built on such stakes holds because every plank was earned, while a zephyr of free throwaway accounts blows away. Forging reputation at scale becomes more expensive than the fraud it would enable.
